newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA FAILS AGAIN AS WEST INDIES BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA FAILS AGAIN AS WEST INDIES BATTLE.

text.p: West Indies recovered from the disappointment of another failure by top batsman Brian Lara to gain a slender advantage over Australia in the third test on Friday.
Lara, the world record holder for the highest scores in test and first-class cricket, fell cheaply after being tormented again by fast bowler Glenn McGrath.
Lara's prized scalp was one of five claimed by McGrath to leave the match delicately poised at close of play on the second day at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
With three days left to play, West Indies are 233 for nine in 103 overs, a lead of 14 runs, in reply to Australia's first innings 219 all out.

Left-hander Jimmy Adams, batting at number six, became the third West Indian after Shivnarine Chanderpaul and wicketkeeper Junior Murray to reach his half-century in the innings and remained unbeaten on 54 at the close.
Lara, who has failed to register a century on tour, scored two before playing a rash cut shot to a wide delivery, slicing a catch to wrist spinner Shane Warne in the gully.

The left-hander, dropped one place down the order to number four because of his indifferent form, has scored a meagre 75 runs at an average of 15 in his last five test innings including one innings of 44 runs.
McGrath, who recorded figures of five for 40 in 27 overs, has totally dominated Lara on tour, a key factor in Australia taking a 2-0 lead in the five-test series.
Resuming on 29 for one, West Indies laboured for runs throughout the day against a relentlessly accurate bowling attack.
Chanderpaul, promoted to number three in the order ahead of Lara, responded well to the challenge by scoring 58 in a resilient innings before scooping a return catch to McGrath.
Murray adopted a more aggressive approach to score 53 before becoming another McGrath victim.
